questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I would like to know more about the culture and lifestyle in a new country, as well as the study pattern

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything provided by the university was clear with detailed instructions; you can get all the information by carefully following the email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international department in our university can help you through the entire process.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student dormitories are randomly assigned to all exchange students, and they are all closely located near campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The canteen is easy to access, with convenient stores on campus. The dorms are also equipped with kitchen for students to make food on their own.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The dorms are clean and cheap, mostly three named Yamate North, Ohmeikan, and Daiko. YN and Ohmeikan are within walking distance, whereas Daiko needs a bit more transportation through the metro. It is mostly international students living in dorms, so it is a great opportunity to meet new friends and cook together!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration is rather flexible, where you can basically choose all the classes you want, with not much of a limitation on major(at least one class from your major). Students should check the deadline for the registration period and submit the form to professors, but 2 weeks of pre-registration period is granted for students to try the classes and finally decide which one they want to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Each student is assigned one supervisor from their department. There are also tutors assigned for students whom you can ask for help from.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: To fulfill the requirements for one semester(30ECTS=15credits), the classes you should take will be around 5-6. The time conflict was a bit hard to manage if you want to choose the Japanese class(but I highly recommend it), but I still managed to fulfill the requirement.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the schedule for classes carefully. If you plan to take the Japanese class, which takes up every morning from Monday to Friday, you need to avoid the time conflict. Participation and attendence are rather important here, so it is better not to skip a lot of classes and plan well. Apart from this, the registration is rather simple and smooth, and hope you can get all the classes you want!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: MA students are mostly restricted to only Master classes based on the difficulty of the courses. Still, the workload is not that heavy as you will mostly have one lecture per week. It should be easy to handle multiple classes at the same time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The workload is indeed heavier than in UCPH. Teachers are more strict with class participation, and the style of teaching varies a lot among professors and departments. Still, the instructors are very nice and there to help, and if you follow the lectures carefully, the materials are rather easy and it won't be hard to pass all the classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Research Skills b [G]; Japanese Culture and Society in Tourism Context [G]; Theme Studies (Statistics for Economics and Business） [G]; Special lecture on Data Science 1 [G]; Special lecture on Data Science 2 [G]; Sustainable Materials Science [G]; NUPACE Japanese 1b

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The NUPACE Japanese! The teachers are all super nice, and you can actually learn the language and culture throughout the semester. The class is kind of intensive as it is held almost every day (for basic levels), but you can see yourself actually improving day by day with all your friends. It would be a fun experience:)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you plan on travelling every weekend, the cost will rise more as little things can add up to quite a lot of spending:) In-store shopping is also enjoyable and irresistible here, so I ended up spending too much...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fruits are really expensive in Japan! Transportation is cheaper than in Denmark, but still rather high, as you may travel a lot (no available monthly tickets for exchange students). Otherwise, everything is within an affordable range.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many cultural and social activities held by clubs, international student clubs, and even dorms. You will have a lot of chances to meet new friends and experience the culture as much as you want!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Activities held by the dorm (Yamate North) were really fun. We had the chance to enjoy the Japanese firework festival, beach party, cooking event, etc.  Also, the weekly gathering by Ace was a good opportunity to make Japanese friends and practice your language.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really love the onsen and sauna in Japan. There are many cheap and wonderful saunas or public baths in Nagoya or nearby cities. It is such a pleasurable experience for relaxation.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Japanese culture is rather different from Western culture. It is always good to keep good manners and stay quiet in public without bothering others too much. Japanese people are generally very nice and easy-going. It won't take long to fit in, but it will take some time.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the student clubs

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People care about behaviors in public a lot. So keeping good manners and trying to avoid bothering others is important but could be hard to follow.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Respect and politeness are something I truly appreciate from Japanese people. I experienced the most during travel.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. travel more whilst you have time, experience the culture by yourself is the best
2. participate more in university activities and make more friends
3. plan your budget well: )

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reach out to professors if you are interested into any research in the school. It would be interesting to join in the lab and work with fellows in the uni.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The many friends I made and the whole experience of Japanese culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to travel as much as possible while keep up with all the classes:) But at the end it worked and paid off.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
